question: The EU directive on empowering consumers for the green transition1 aims to facilitate sustainable consumption by ensuring that consumers have access to clear and reliable information about the environmental impact of products. The new directive amends two existing consumer law directives: the Consumer Rights Directive2 and the Unfair Commercial Practices Directive3.

According to the Commission’s interpretation, all non-compliant environmental labels and claims must be removed from consumer communication from that date, irrespective of when the product was placed on the market.

However, national transposition is still ongoing in most Member States, leaving businesses uncertain about which claims and labels will fall under the directive’s scope, meaning traders will have very limited time to adapt. The removal or destruction of non-compliant products could result in massive economic losses and unnecessary food waste, which would contradict the directive’s environmental objectives.
In this context: 1.
Will the Commission allow a sell-through period for products placed on the market before 27 September 2026?
Will the Commission issue harmonised guidance on the scope of claims and labels covered?
Will the Commission ensure consistent and proportionate enforcement across Member States to avoid market disruption and to prevent further environmental harm?

Directive (EU) 2024/825 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 28 February 2024 amending Directives 2005/29/EC and 2011/83/EU as regards empowering consumers for the green transition through better protection against unfair practices and through better information (OJ L, 2024/825, 6.3.2024, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2024/825/oj).

European Commission, ‘Consumer rights directive’, European Commission website, https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/consumer-protection-law/consumer-contract-law/consumerrights-directive_en. European Commission, Unfair commercial practices directive’, European Commission website, https://commission.europa.
eu/law/law-topic/consumer-protection-law/unfair-commercial-practices-and-priceindication/unfair-commercial-practices-directive_en.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.2.2026) As the Commission set out in its reply to written question E-004392/20251, Directive (EU) 2024/825 on empowering consumers for the green transition2 introduced targeted amendments of the Unfair Commercial Practices Directive3 (UCPD).

Directive (EU) 2024/825 entered into force on 26 March 2024, will have to be transposed by 27 March 2026 and will become applicable from 27 September 2026. From that date, traders will need to ensure that their environmental claims and sustainability labels in a business-to-consumer context comply with the new provisions, including for existing products.

The UCPD does not regulate the placing of products on the market but focuses exclusively on how they are presented to consumers, such as through marketing. To facilitate a coherent application, the Commission has published a Questions & Answers document4.

Enforcement lies with national authorities, and they will investigate and prioritise enforcement actions according to the gravity and the circumstances of each case. Authorities may assess, for example, whether traders have made reasonable and proportionate efforts to comply, including for products already in the distribution chain, taking due account of proportionality, legal certainty and legitimate expectations.

The Commission is discussing this matter with national authorities to support a fair and effective enforcement across the EU. At a workshop with national authorities on 27 January 2026, business and consumer associations were also invited, contributing to a constructive and useful exchange5.
